You carry two copies of APOE ε2, the rarest common version of this gene; about 1 in 160 people of European ancestry have this pair. Each ε2 copy is linked to a longer life: about 28 % higher odds of reaching the top 10 % of ages in a large European study, and about 7 months more lifespan per copy in UK and European family data. A study of long-lived people found higher odds of extreme old age for people with ε2/ε2 or ε2/ε3 than with the common ε3/ε3. The figure for two copies is an estimate built from single copies, and direct data on this rare pair are thin and uncertain. ε2/ε2 also has downsides, below. For Alzheimer's disease, see the second result for this pair and the separate APOE module. A tendency, not destiny.
